papers.title: Word Length and Diameter in Permutation Groups
papers.abstract: In the binary diameter problem, the input consists of explicitly given permutations generating a finite group $G$ and a binary-encoded number $k$, and the question is whether every element of $G$ is a product of at most $k$ of the given generators. In the binary length problem, the input additionally contains a permutation $g \in G$, and the question is whether $g$ is such a product. We show that the binary diameter problem is PSPACE-complete, thereby confirming a conjecture of Lohrey and Rosowski (2023). Moreover, we show that PSPACE-hardness already holds for solvable groups of derived length at most 3, whereas the problem is $\Pi_2^{\mathrm{P}}$-complete for 2-step nilpotent groups. For the binary length problem, we establish a sharp complexity threshold: the problem is NP-complete for 2-step nilpotent groups, which extends a result of Lohrey and Rosowski for abelian groups, and PSPACE-complete for groups that are simultaneously 3-step nilpotent and metabelian, which strengthens the main result of Jerrum (1985). Finally, we show that the unary diameter problem, where $k$ is encoded in unary, is $\Pi_2^{\mathrm{P}}$-complete for generating sets of the full symmetric group, confirming another conjecture of Lohrey and Rosowski.

papers.title: Profinite approach to S-adic shift spaces II: Invertible directive sequences
papers.abstract: This paper is the second in a series about (relatively) free profinite semigroups and S-adic representations of minimal shifts. The first installment introduced the key notions of profinite images and saturating properties. The present paper examines the relationship between relative invertibility conditions (on a directive sequence) and charging properties (of a shift). The main result shows that the two properties are equivalent under mild conditions. Moreover, charging properties are shown to be equivalent to density of subgroups generated by return words in relatively free profinite groups. The main result can then be used to deduce purely discrete statements about subgroups generated by return words in relatively free groups. We also highlight applications of the main result to the study of maximal bifix decoding, following earlier work by the second author. Finally, we establish some results on the effect of direct images on charging properties and explain how to apply these results to the case of episturmian shifts.

papers.title: Separately continuous maps into regular spaces and continuity of operations in separable semitopological groups
papers.abstract: A space is feebly compact if every locally finite family of nonempty open subsets of it is finite; a Tychonoff space is feebly compact if and only if it is pseudocompact. M. Tkachenko asked whether a regular feebly compact semitopological group is a topological group provided that it is separable, has countable tightness, or is a $k$-space; for Tychonoff groups the answer is known to be positive. We answer this question in the separable case: every regular separable feebly compact semitopological group is a topological group. The proof is based on the following result: if $X$ is a separable Baire space, $Y$ is a feebly compact space and $Z$ is a regular space, then every separately continuous map $X\times Y\to Z$ is strongly quasicontinuous. Unlike the known approaches for Tychonoff spaces, the proof does not use real-valued functions. More generally, every regular separable semitopological group which is $\Gamma^{BM}_o$-nonmeager, a Baire-type property defined by a modification of the Banach-Mazur game, is a topological group. This class of groups contains all regular separable Baire groups which are feebly $p$-spaces; feebly $p$-spaces form a wider class of spaces, which contains all feebly compact spaces and all $p$-spaces. The results remain valid for spaces satisfying the assumptions locally. In particular, every regular locally separable locally feebly compact semitopological group is a topological group.

papers.title: Odd-ordered Cayley graphs satisfy Erd\H{o}s--Gy\'arf\'as
papers.abstract: Erd\H{o}s and Gy\'arf\'as conjectured that every graph with minimum degree at least three contains a power-of-two-length cycle. We prove every Cayley graph of odd order satisfies the conjecture. As a corollary, we find that Cayley graphs of finite nilpotent groups satisfy the conjecture as well.

papers.title: Invariant random subgroups of the finitary special linear group over a finite field
papers.abstract: An invariant random subgroup of a discrete group is a conjugation-invariant probability measure on the space of its subgroups. We confirm a conjecture of Simon Thomas and classify the invariant random subgroups of the finitary special and general linear groups over a finite field. These are shown to be stabilizers of random tuples of vectors and functionals. The classification uses the character theory of the finitary special linear group established by Skudlarek and the theory of the invariant random subgroups of the finitary permutation group established by Vershik. In addition, we classify the invariant probability measures for several natural actions of these finitary groups.

papers.title: Remarks on the Farthing--Muhly--Yeend inverse semigroup of a finitely aligned higher-rank graph
papers.abstract: Given a finitely aligned higher-rank $k$-graph $\Lambda$, Farthing, Muhly and Yeend (Semigroup Forum 2005) constructed an inverse semigroup $S_\Lambda$ to provide a groupoid model for the $C^*$-algebra of $\Lambda$. In this paper, we extend some of the existing results related to the semigroup structure of a graph inverse semigroup to the more general setting of the inverse semigroup $S_\Lambda$. We obtain geometric descriptions of the Green's relations on $S_\Lambda$, which effectively generalize the existing characterization of Green's relations on a graph inverse semigroup. We provide a simple and useful description of the Cuntz-Krieger ideal of the Booleanization of $S_\Lambda$ and, based on this, identify a certain $X$-to-join Booleanization of $S_\Lambda$, where the abstract and concrete Cuntz-Krieger relations agree. Besides the natural partial order, $S_\Lambda$ is also ordered by set-inclusion. This helps us to realize $S_\Lambda$ as a semigroup \emph{graded-ordered} by $\mathbb{Z}^k$ and, subsequently, gives rise to a full inverse subsemigroup $S_\Lambda^h$ of $S_\Lambda$, which is graded by $\mathbb{Z}^k$ in the usual sense. We show that the Kumjian-Pask algebra of $\Lambda$ is graded isomorphic to the quotient of the contracted semigroup algebra of $S_\Lambda^h$ by the tight ideal. In the final part of the paper, we show that a $k$-graph morphism $p:\Lambda_1\longrightarrow \Lambda_2$ that is injective and satisfies a certain path lifting property induces, in a natural way, an injective $0$-preserving semigroup homomorphism from $S_{\Lambda_1}$ to $S_{\Lambda_2}$. In view of this, we build a suitable categorical setup to conclude that the isomorphism established between the Kumjian-Pask algebra of $\Lambda$ and the tight ideal quotient of the semigroup algebra of $S_\Lambda^h$ is natural.

papers.title: $L^2$-Betti numbers of Dehn fillings
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of the $L^2$-Betti numbers of group-theoretic Dehn fillings. For a broad class of virtually special groups $G$, we prove that the $L^2$-Betti numbers of sufficiently deep Dehn fillings $\overline{G}$ are equal to those of $G$. As applications, we verify the Singer Conjecture for certain Einstein manifolds, establish a virtual fibering criterion for $\overline{G}$, obtain bounds on deficiency of $\overline{G}$, and provide new examples of hyperbolic groups with exotic subgroups that arise as Dehn fillings of any cusped arithmetic hyperbolic manifold of dimension at least four.

papers.title: Finite groups with all involutions fused
papers.abstract: We characterize finite groups whose involutions form a single fusion class. In the solvable case, we show that the $2$-length is $1$, extending Thompson's theorem which states that a solvable group with all involutions conjugate has $2$-length $1$. For a nonsolvable group $G$, we prove that if its involutions are fused then they are conjugate; moreover, $G/\mathbf{O}_{2'}(G)$ is almost quasisimple. As an application, we obtain a restriction on $m$ for which an $m$-pyramidal Kirkman triple system can be realized under a nonsolvable group.

papers.title: A surface-group action on real-hyperbolic space with no Cannon--Thurston map
papers.abstract: We present discrete, faithful and purely loxodromic representations of a closed surface group of genus 431, and of a free group, into the group of isometries of a finite-dimensional real-hyperbolic space for which no Cannon--Thurston map exists. The construction combines three ingredients: the small-cancellation strategy employed by Baker--Riley to construct a subgroup of an ambient hyperbolic group with no Cannon--Thurston map, the realization of these groups by octagon complexes, and a theorem of Desgroseilliers--Haglund that supplies a convex cocompact faithful representation of the ambient hyperbolic group on a real-hyperbolic space. These examples admit ray Cannon--Thurston maps, as defined by Halder, Mahan Mj and Sardar.

papers.title: Finiteness properties of centralisers in $\mathrm{Out}(F_N)$ and automorphisms of free-by-cyclic groups
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group. We prove that the centraliser of any element of $\mathrm{Out}(F)$ or $\mathrm{Aut}(F)$ is of type $\rm{VF}$. We also prove that the (outer) automorphism group of any free-by-cyclic group $M=F\rtimes_\varphi\mathbb{Z}$ is of type $\rm{VF}$, and so are the McCool subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(M)$. This relies on the construction of a new $\mathrm{Out}(M)$-invariant splitting of $M$, that enables us to reduce the proof of the above statements to the case where the outer class of $\varphi$ has finite order.

papers.title: Kaplansky's conjectures fail for torsion-free hyperbolic groups in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Do Kaplansky's group-ring conjectures hold for torsion-free word-hyperbolic groups? We show that all four fail in positive characteristic. For every prime $p$ there is a finitely presented, torsion-free, word-hyperbolic group $G$ with a finite two-dimensional classifying space and $a,b\in\mathbb{F}_p[G]$ with $ab=1\neq ba$. So, over every field of characteristic $p$, the group algebra of $G$ is not directly finite and has a non-trivial idempotent, zero divisor and unit, and $G$ is neither sofic nor surjunctive. For $p=2$, $G$, $a$ and $b$ come from OpenAI's random construction, and we add that $G$ is hyperbolic with probability $1-o(1)$, as are OpenAI's zero-divisor groups. For odd $p$ the groups are new: they adapt OpenAI's direct-finiteness construction with a signed cancellation, found first by S. V. Ivanov and independently by us, via an exact solution of a colour-balance problem and a Perron certificate. As far as we know, they are the first torsion-free counterexamples to direct finiteness and to the idempotent conjecture in odd characteristic. Hyperbolicity comes from one deterministic criterion: if a labelled graph is pattern-free, the group obtained by coning off its components is aspherical and has a linear isoperimetric inequality. We prove it by running OpenAI's exclusion of reduced spheres on van Kampen discs, an accounting OpenAI used for another complex. For every prime $p$, the existence of $G$, $a$ and $b$ and the failure of all four conjectures are formalized in Lean 4, including existence forms of the random-graph estimates used. In characteristic zero, where the idempotent and direct-finiteness conjectures hold for torsion-free hyperbolic groups, we show that no cancellation built into the vertex types survives the decay estimate that makes the groups torsion-free. OpenAI's characteristic-two counterexample with torsion is a CAT(0) group.

papers.title: Chordality of Enhanced Power Graphs of Finite Simple Groups: A Resolution of a Conjecture
papers.abstract: The \emph{enhanced power graph} $\PE(G)$ of a finite group $G$ has vertex set $G$, two elements being adjacent if and only if they generate a cyclic subgroup. We determine the finite simple groups $G$ for which $\PE(G)$ is chordal: they are the cyclic groups of prime order, $\Alt(7)$, $\PSL_2(q)$ ($q\ge4$), $\Sz(q)$ ($q=2^{2n+1}\ge8$) and $\PSL_3(4)$. This answers an open problem of Bubboloni, Fumagalli and Praeger \cite{BFP}. We also prove that for every finite group $G$, if the power graph $P(G)$ is a cograph (resp.\ chordal) then so is $\PE(G)$; the cograph case is a conjecture of Bubboloni, Fumagalli and Praeger \cite{BFP}.

papers.title: Alperin weight bijections and dimensions of simple modules
papers.abstract: We propose a new refinement of the (blockwise) Alperin weight conjecture taking dimensions of simple modules (or degrees of irreducible Brauer characters) into consideration. This is similar to Giannelli's refinement of the (Alperin--)McKay conjecture. We prove this new refinement for blocks with a cyclic or Klein four defect group, for inertial blocks (which include the Brou\'{e}--Puig nilpotent blocks), and for $p$-blocks of $p$-solvable groups.

papers.title: Morse accessibility with applications to Coxeter groups
papers.abstract: In this paper we begin developing a theory of Morse hierarchies for finitely generated groups. Very roughly, a Morse hierarchy is a iterative splitting of a group over subgroups that do not contribute to the Morse boundary of the ambient group. We apply this theory to Coxeter groups, establishing new combinatorial criteria that distinguish certain Coxeter groups from other Coxeter groups as well as right-angled Artin groups up to quasi-isometry. We highlight the consequences for the right-angled case. To build the reader's intuition, the last section provides many examples of Morse hierarchies and their subtleties. Finally, there is an appendix by the second author and Vivian He that extends these ideas to the metrizable Cashen--Mackay topology on the Morse boundary.

papers.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $\Lambda=\pi_1^{alg}(G)$, the Galois group $\Theta=Gal(L/K)$ acting on $\Lambda$, where $L$ is a finite Galois extension of $K$ having no real places, the decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v\subseteq \Theta$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. We also compute $Sha^S(K,G)$ in some cases where $S$ contains archimedean places.

papers.title: An Ito-Michler type theorem and the prime class graph of weakly integral braided fusion categories
papers.abstract: In a weakly integral braided fusion category, a prime divides none of the conjugacy-class dimensions if and only if it does not divide the Frobenius-Perron dimension of the adjoint subcategory. We prove that these conditions hold precisely when the corresponding Sylow subgroup of the group of invertible objects generates a braided Deligne factor whose dimension is the largest power of that prime dividing the Frobenius-Perron dimension of the category. We also prove that the prime graph of the conjugacy-class dimensions has at most two connected components. If the graph is disconnected, the category is solvable. The bound is attained by the representation category of the Drinfeld double of the symmetric group on three letters.

papers.title: Decompositions of homomorphisms of abelian $p$-groups with $p^2$-bounded target
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime. We classify homomorphisms $H:V_1\to V_2$ between abelian $p$-groups that are direct sums of cyclic groups, under the assumption $p^2V_2=0$. We prove that every such homomorphism is isomorphic to a direct sum of finite indecomposable representations and that this decomposition is unique up to isomorphism and reordering of the summands.

papers.title: Density of finitely supported invariant measures for automorphisms of compact abelian groups
papers.abstract: We study the structure of invariant measures for continuous automorphisms of compact metrizable abelian groups satisfying the descending chain condition. We show that the finitely supported invariant measures are weak-* dense in the space of all invariant probability measures, and that if the system is ergodic with respect to Haar measure, then the finitely supported ergodic invariant measures are also dense. A key ingredient in the proof is a variant of the specification property, which we establish for the ergodic systems in this class. Our results also yield the following two consequences: first, that every finitely generated group that is a semidirect product of $\mathbb{Z}$ with a countable abelian group $G$ is Hilbert-Schmidt stable; and second, a Livshitz-type theorem characterizing the uniform closure of coboundaries arising from continuous functions in terms of vanishing on periodic orbits. We also construct an example showing that, in general dynamical systems, the property of having dense finitely supported invariant measures does not pass to product systems.

papers.title: The Fundamental Semigroup and Associative Lifts of Topological Semigroups
papers.abstract: We introduce the fundamental semigroup $\Lambda(S)$ of a nonempty path-connected topological semigroup $S$, defined using right translations and change-of-basepoint isomorphisms on its fundamental group. We prove that this construction is closed under composition and independent of the chosen basepoint up to isomorphism. It is also invariant under homotopy equivalences that preserve multiplication up to homotopy. We characterize exactly when the fundamental semigroup is a group and identify that group with an inner automorphism group. For a connected, locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected topological semigroup, we show that multiplication admits a continuous associative lift to the universal cover if and only if $\Lambda(S)$ contains an idempotent. Every such idempotent can be realized by an associative lift, and any two associative lifts are isomorphic over $S$ through a deck transformation. We obtain existence results when the fundamental group has finite inner automorphism group or contains no subgroup isomorphic to Thompson's group $F$, and when the underlying space is a finite-dimensional CW complex. In contrast, we construct a path-connected countable CW topological semigroup with cells in arbitrarily high dimensions whose multiplication admits no continuous associative lift to its universal cover.

papers.title: On a Completion of Cohomological Functors Generalising Tate Cohomology I
papers.abstract: Tate cohomology has been generalised by several authors using different constructions that have applications in group theory, ring theory and homotopical algebra. Therefore, there is a need for a uniform account that explains why their underlying approaches all lead to the same conclusions. The key notion in such a uniform theory is a specific completion of cohomological functors that is constructed under mild assumptions. This completion takes Tate cohomology to settings where it has never been introduced such as in condensed mathematics. Through the latter, one can define Tate cohomology for any $T1$ topological group.

papers.title: On Zappa-Sz\'ep products of two semidihedral groups
papers.abstract: Let $n, m \ge 4$. We study the Zappa--Sz\'ep products $G = HK$ with $H = \langle x\rangle \rtimes \langle y\rangle \cong SD_{2^n}$ and $K = \langle z\rangle \rtimes \langle w\rangle \cong SD_{2^m}$, together with the fixed generators $x, y, z, w$, and we describe the parameter tuples which encode the mixed commutators of these generators, according to the cores of $\langle x\rangle$ and $\langle z\rangle$ in~$G$. First, when both $\langle x\rangle$ and $\langle z\rangle$ are normal in~$G$, we show that the admissible parameter tuples are exactly the solutions of an explicit system of six polynomial congruences. Second, when the cores $\langle x\rangle_G$ and $\langle z\rangle_G$ are arbitrary subgroups of $\langle x\rangle$ and $\langle z\rangle$, under the simplifying assumption $[x, z] = 1$, and for generating systems for which all mixed commutators lie in $\langle x\rangle\langle z\rangle$, we obtain an analogous classification by twelve congruences together with two order conditions; this is the semidihedral counterpart of the Hu--Yu classification~\cite{HuYu2025} for dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ and $D_{2m}$ with $n, m$ odd. In contrast with that case, we further construct an explicit exact product with both cores non-trivial and $[x, z] \ne 1$, so that the semidihedral setting contains additional families of exact products.

papers.title: On quandles with isomorphic enveloping groups
papers.abstract: We give a method to construct two injective connected finite quandles of different cardinal with isomorphic enveloping groups.
